The symbolic constructs form a causal chain where stimulus energy initiates neural processing, leading to reaction potential and eventual habit formation. Each link maintains a dual role: observable event and latent variable. Neural interaction (&) mediates complex stimulus integration, while reinforcement (G) modulates future behavior. Drive strength (D) motivates action, and inhibition (Ie) prevents maladaptive responses. Oscillation (sOe) introduces temporal dynamics. The system operates under probabilistic thresholds (aLe), enabling stochastic evolution of behavior. Failure modes include insufficient stimulus energy, lack of reinforcement, or excessive inhibition. These primitives define a closed-loop dynamical system with feedback mechanisms.
